label: Hamilton Lodge Ball
detail: Described as the first recorded drag ball in US history.

label: Anti-Saloon League founded
detail: The single-issue prohibition group starts in Oberlin, Ohio, and goes national after 1895.

label: State takes control of Boston's Licensing Board
detail: Chapter 291 of the Acts of 1906 makes the board's three members governor-appointed.

label: National Prohibition begins
detail: The Eighteenth Amendment takes effect, one year after ratification.

label: New York City cabaret law
detail: A license is now required for music, singing or dancing where food or drink is sold.

label: Cocoanut Grove opens
detail: The nightclub opens at 17 Piedmont Street, near Park Square.

label: Liquor license quota created
detail: Post-Prohibition law gives Boston 1,000 on-premises and 350 off-premises licenses by population.

label: Prohibition repealed
detail: The Twenty-first Amendment ends federal prohibition, following March's 3.2% beer and wine law.

label: Jacques Restaurant opens in Boston
detail: Later a gay bar, described as Boston's oldest continuously operating gay bar.

label: Cocoanut Grove fire
detail: A fire at the nightclub kills 492 people, the deadliest disaster in Boston's history per the city.

label: Cocoanut Grove fire, Boston
detail: 490 or 492 die in an overcrowded club with locked exits and a jammed revolving door; codes add outward-swinging doors, lit exit signs and revolving-door rules.

label: West Berlin abolishes its Sperrstunde
detail: Allied commandants vote 2 to 1 to end closing time, after lobbying by hotelier Heinz Zellermayer

label: GDR caps East Berlin hours
detail: Midnight on weekdays, 1 a.m. on Saturdays

label: Title II of the Civil Rights Act
detail: US law bars race, color, religion and national-origin discrimination in places of entertainment.

label: Stonewall Inn raid
detail: Police raid begins around 1:15 a.m., starting the riot seen as the catalyst of the modern LGBT civil rights movement.

label: Stonewall uprising
detail: A police raid on a Greenwich Village gay bar sparks several nights of riots and demonstrations.

label: Studio 54's 'perfect salad'
detail: Steve Rubell's door at Studio 54 sets the template for the curated door.

label: The Loft's first party
detail: David Mancuso's "Love Saves The Day" at 647 Broadway, New York.

label: House of LaBeija founded
detail: Founded in Harlem by Lottie and Crystal LaBeija (some sources say 1977).

label: Combat Zone approved
detail: The Boston Zoning Commission approves an official adult entertainment district on lower Washington Street.

label: Frankie Knuckles at the Warehouse
detail: Knuckles becomes resident DJ at the Chicago club that gave house music its name.

label: Paradise Garage opens
detail: Michael Brody's members-only, no-alcohol club opens officially at 84 King Street, with Larry Levan as resident.

label: Disco Demolition Night
detail: Records are blown up at Comiskey Park, Chicago; about 7,000 fans storm the field.

label: Massachusetts bans happy hour
detail: The state bars free and discounted drink specials as a drunk-driving measure.

label: Koire v. Metro Car Wash
detail: California Supreme Court rules sex-based discounts, including ladies' nights, violate the Unruh Act.

label: "Techno!" and the second summer of love
detail: A UK compilation names the Detroit sound as the acid house boom peaks.

label: Bottle service in Paris
detail: Les Bains Douches offers table reservations with a bottle, according to VinePair.

label: Happy Land fire, Bronx
detail: Arson at an illegal social club with no certificate of occupancy kills 87; both exits were at the front.

label: Paris Is Burning premieres
detail: Jennie Livingston's ballroom documentary premieres at Toronto; it wins the Sundance Grand Jury Prize in 1991.

label: Tresor opens in Berlin
detail: A techno club in the vaults of the former Wertheim department store becomes the Berlin hub of Detroit techno.

label: Bottle service reaches New York
detail: The Tunnel introduces bottle service at $90 a bottle, when a drink cost $6.

label: "Repetitive beats" law
detail: The UK Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 receives royal assent.

label: Mixmag on DJ fees
detail: Mixmag reports top UK DJs asking £8,000-£15,000 for New Year's Eve.

label: fabric starts a no-photo policy
detail: London club bans photos and video on its dancefloors; later lapses and is reinstated before 2021.

label: Private Security Industry Act
detail: UK law behind the SIA door supervisor licence.

label: California limits swiped ID data
detail: Civil Code 1798.90.1 bars keeping swiped license data except for listed purposes.

label: Berlin plans weekend all-night U-Bahn
detail: BVG submitted plans for continuous weekend night service, targeted for the June 2003 timetable change.

label: E2 crowd crush, Chicago
detail: 21 die on the only open stairway after pepper spray is used on a fight.

label: The Station fire, West Warwick, Rhode Island
detail: Band pyrotechnics ignite foam in an unsprinklered club; 100 die.

label: NYC smoking ban reaches bars and clubs
detail: Pushed by Mayor Michael Bloomberg, it extends to all workplaces.

label: Rhode Island Comprehensive Fire Safety Act
detail: Ends grandfathering; sprinklers required in clubs over 150 by 2006; indoor pyrotechnics largely banned.

label: NFPA emergency amendments
detail: Sprinklers in new nightclubs and existing ones over 100; crowd managers in all assembly occupancies.

label: SIA licence fee set
detail: UK door supervisor licence fee set at £190, still unchanged as of 2023.

label: Massachusetts nightclub fire safety law
detail: Sprinklers for clubs of 100 or more within three years; criminal penalties for blocked exits and overcrowding.

label: NFPA 101 2006 edition issued
detail: Nightclub sprinkler rules made permanent in the Life Safety Code and NFPA 5000.

label: Licensing Act 2003 takes effect in England and Wales
detail: Fixed closing times end; premises are licensed for set hours, up to 24.

label: England and Wales end the 11 p.m. pub close
detail: The Licensing Act 2003 takes effect at midnight, allowing flexible hours set per premises

label: NYC 'Bouncer Bill' signed
detail: City may close venues with unlicensed or unchecked security staff.

label: Milwaukee nightclub consent decree
detail: Justice Department settles race-based door refusal case.

label: Avalon and Axis demolished
detail: The 15 Lansdowne Street club building comes down; a concert hall opens on the site in 2009.

label: England bans smoking in pubs and clubs
detail: Health Act 2006 takes effect at 06:00 BST.

label: Newcastle, NSW imposes 3:30 a.m. close and 1:30 a.m. lockout
detail: Applied to 14 central venues; monthly assaults later fell from 33 to 22.

label: Berlin smoking law in force
detail: Bans smoking in clubs except in enclosed smoking rooms; a 2009 amendment adds a small-bar exception.

label: Virginia Beach nightspot consent decree
detail: Justice Department settles case over a hairstyle-based dress code.

label: Newcastle, NSW restricts late trading
detail: 3:30 a.m. close and 1:30 a.m. lockout for 14 city-center venues

label: Paris sets bar closing between 2 and 5 a.m.
detail: Police-prefect order; later hours by exception

label: Amsterdam lets two nightlife areas stay open later
detail: Researchers later linked each extra hour to about 34% more alcohol-related ambulance call-outs.

label: France sets 7 a.m. nightclub limit
detail: Decree 2009-1652; no alcohol sales in the last 90 minutes

label: Equality Act 2010
detail: UK law bars service providers from discriminatory refusal of service.

label: Vienna starts all-night weekend U-Bahn
detail: Followed a February 2010 city poll with 54% in favor.

label: Hawaii limits ID barcode scanning
detail: HRS 487J restricts what venues may scan and keep.

label: The Loop starts non-public drug testing in nightclubs
detail: Festival testing followed from 2014; public pilots ran 2016 to 2018.

label: Kiss nightclub fire, Santa Maria, Brazil
detail: Outdoor flares ignite ceiling foam; 242 die.

label: Good Night Out co-founded
detail: Bryony Beynon starts the venue staff-training campaign on sexual harassment.

label: Glasgow disability door ruling
detail: Sheriff Court upholds discrimination claim by a couple refused entry.

label: MBTA late-night pilot begins
detail: Weekend subway and 15 bus routes ran until about 2:30 a.m.; the pilot ended in 2016 over cost.

label: Sydney lockout and last-drinks reforms
detail: A 2019 evaluation found assaults down sharply in Kings Cross but up in nearby areas.

label: Sydney lockout laws take effect
detail: 1:30 a.m. lockout and 3 a.m. last drinks in the CBD precinct and Kings Cross

label: Late Night T begins
detail: The MBTA starts a pilot of weekend subway and bus service until about 2:30 a.m.

label: Boston gets 75 licenses and its own board
detail: A state economic development bill adds licenses and lets the mayor appoint the Licensing Board.

label: Marquardt calls the Berghain door 'subjective'
detail: Interview with GQ, reported by Mixmag.

label: Vegas superclubs top $100 million
detail: XS and Hakkasan each gross over $100 million a year, per Nightclub & Bar.

label: Colectiv fire, Bucharest
detail: Pyrotechnics ignite foam in a club licensed for 80; 64 die and the government resigns.

label: Ask for Angela launches
detail: Code-phrase scheme starts in Lincolnshire, England; expands across London in August 2021.

label: Ask for Angela launched in Lincolnshire
detail: Created by Hayley Crawford; later spread across the UK and abroad.

label: Late Night T voted out
detail: The MBTA's control board votes 4-0 to end late-night service; last runs about March 18.

label: MBTA board votes to end late-night weekend service
detail: The 4-0 vote ended Boston's 2014 pilot, citing maintenance time and cost.

label: Record DJ earnings
detail: Calvin Harris earns an estimated $63 million in 12 months, a Guinness record based on Forbes.

label: Japan allows all-night dancing
detail: Fueiho amendment lets clubs above 10 lux open 24 hours outside residential areas

label: Stonewall National Monument designated
detail: President Obama signs Proclamation 9465.

label: London Night Tube launches
detail: Central and Victoria lines first, with Jubilee, Northern and Piccadilly that autumn.

label: Brazil publishes Lei Kiss
detail: Law 13.425/2017 sets national fire rules for places of public assembly, with 12 vetoes.

label: Massachusetts casinos get 4 a.m.
detail: State budget signed by Gov. Charlie Baker allows casino service until 4 a.m.

label: New York repeals the cabaret law
detail: Mayor de Blasio signs the repeal after a 44-1 council vote on October 31.

label: Gov. Jerry Brown vetoes California SB 905
detail: "Enough mischief from midnight to 2"; the only one of Wiener's four bills to reach a veto

label: New York publishes its first nightlife economic study
detail: $35.1 billion in output and 299,000 jobs, using 2016 data.

label: NYC natural hair guidance
detail: Commission on Human Rights says nightclubs cannot bar natural hairstyles.

label: Bars close in the New York area
detail: New York, New Jersey and Connecticut end on-premises bar and restaurant service at 8 p.m.

label: UK clubs ordered closed
detail: Nightclubs and music venues in the UK are ordered to close.

label: New York subway closes overnight
detail: First overnight closure in its 116-year history, for COVID cleaning.

label: Culture Recovery Fund announced
detail: The UK announces a £1.57 billion Culture Recovery Fund.

label: First Culture Recovery round
detail: £257 million goes to 1,300+ English organizations; the NTIA says few dance clubs were funded.

label: Lesbian Bar Project launches
detail: Counts 15 lesbian bars in the US, down from about 200 in the 1980s.

label: SVOG created
detail: Congress passes $15 billion for the Shuttered Venue Operators Grant.

label: UK spiking reports peak
detail: Police-recorded spiking reports peaked in autumn 2021.

label: SVOG portal crashes
detail: The SVOG application portal opens, crashes, and reopens April 26.

label: New York restores 24-hour subway service
detail: Service resumed at 2 a.m.

label: England's clubs reopen
detail: Nightclubs in England reopen at midnight after closing in March 2020.

label: SIA top-up training
detail: Renewal requires counter-terror, emergency and first aid training.

label: GHB moved to Class B in the UK
detail: One of the measures listed in the Home Office spiking report.

label: SVOG totals
detail: The SBA reports $14.57 billion in SVOG awards.

label: California SB 930 stalls
detail: 28 yes, 29 no on the Assembly floor, needing 41

label: Itaewon crowd crush, Seoul
detail: 159 killed in the alleys of a nightlife district on Halloween weekend.

label: Berlin inspections find poor smoking compliance
detail: District inspections report a high need for action in many clubs.

label: Miami Beach rolls back South of Fifth to 2 a.m.
detail: Venues over 100 capacity lose 5 a.m. sales; a judge upholds the rule

label: First Director of Nightlife Economy
detail: Corean Reynolds starts as Boston's first nightlife director.

label: Massachusetts senators push to fund test kits
detail: State senators sought kits for nightlife venues; DPH says none were bought.

label: $600,000 Boston license
detail: A Boston full-bar liquor license sells for $600,000.

label: UK's first licensed regular drug checking service opens
detail: The Loop, Home Office-licensed and council-commissioned, in Bristol.

label: 225 new Boston licenses
detail: Gov. Healey signs a law creating 225 licenses, mostly non-transferable and neighborhood-restricted.

label: UK nightclub count falls
detail: NTIA counts 835 UK nightclubs, down from 1,240 in March 2020.

label: Massachusetts DPH reports against bulk-buying test kits
detail: Report to the Legislature favored awareness campaigns and staff bystander training.

label: First new neighborhood licenses issued
detail: Boston awards 37 restricted licenses in Mattapan, Roxbury, Hyde Park and East Boston.

label: Berlin door study
detail: Journal of Marketing study 'Curating the Crowd' decodes Berlin door selection.

label: T runs about an hour later on weekends
detail: Subway and some bus service extended on Friday and Saturday nights as a permanent schedule change.

label: MBTA runs subway about an hour later on weekends
detail: All four lines run later on Friday and Saturday nights, at about $2 million a year.

label: MBTA adds about an hour of weekend service
detail: Subway and some bus and Silver Line routes run later Friday and Saturday nights.

label: Sober Sunday party draws a queue in Berlin
detail: The Observer reports a 6 p.m. line for an alcohol-free party edition.

label: Berlin break-even share falls
detail: Clubcommission survey: 61% of Berlin clubs break even, down from 79% in 2017 (secondary summary).

label: NSW abolishes the last lockout-era rules
detail: Twelve years to the day after the lockouts were announced

label: London Nightlife Taskforce reports
detail: 23 recommendations, including an independent Nightlife Commission.

label: UK spiking offence becomes law
detail: The Crime and Policing Act, creating an offence of administering a harmful substance, received Royal Assent.

label: 3 a.m. last call for the summer
detail: A temporary state law lets eligible Boston bars serve to 3 a.m. through July 31, 2026; a council measure for permanent 3 a.m. follows in late June.

label: Massachusetts temporary 3 a.m. option
detail: Opt-in extra hour for cities and towns, expiring at the end of July 2026

label: Ontario allows 4 a.m. for the World Cup
detail: Bars and restaurants may sell until 4 a.m. through July 19, 2026
